Package frc.robot.subsystems.arm

Class ArmConstants

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.subsystems.arm.ArmConstants
public class ArmConstants extends Object
The physical description of one arm, supplied to the IO that models or drives it.

These values come from CAD, from a team's own measurements, or from a previous robot. They are properties of a mechanism, not of the robot, which is why they are passed into the IO rather than being global constants the library owns: a team with two arms constructs two of these, and a team reusing this library on a different robot writes its own values without editing the library. 


 ArmConstants constants = new ArmConstants()
     .withMotor(DCMotor.getKrakenX60(1))
     .withGearRatio(100.0)
     .withArmLength(Meters.of(0.6))
     .withArmMass(Kilogram.of(5.0))
     .withTravel(Rotations.of(-0.05), Rotations.of(0.5));

Why a mutable class with fluent setters. Java has no named arguments, so a twelve-parameter constructor would be unreadable and trivially mis-ordered. Every setter returns this and validates its input, which makes a mis-specified mechanism fail immediately at construction with a useful message instead of producing strange motion later.

Subclassing. A team that needs extra fields can extend this class. Consumers read through the accessors, so overridden values are honoured.

    • withTravel

      public ArmConstants withTravel(edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Angle minAngle, edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Angle maxAngle)
      Sets both travel limits at once, which also validates that they are ordered.

      Setting them together rather than individually is what makes an inverted range impossible to construct through this API. A stowed arm often sits slightly below horizontal, so a small negative lower limit is normal.

      Parameters:
      minAngle - the lower limit, measured from the zero position
      maxAngle - the upper limit, measured from the zero position
      Returns:
      this, for chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if minAngle is not below maxAngle

    • withGoalTolerance

      public ArmConstants withGoalTolerance(edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Angle goalTolerance)
      Sets the tolerance within which the arm counts as at its target.

      Sized for a mechanism held by a software loop rather than a servo: a proportional loop settles slowly near the end of a move, so an unrealistically tight tolerance would leave atGoal() false for a long time.

      Parameters:
      goalTolerance - the tolerance
      Returns:
      this, for chaining
